tags.description: Typed associative thought bubble (source: NPL thought blocks) — a display-only container whose typed children are `npl-thought` tags carrying a `type` attribute, one per NPL thought-block type (`src/lit/npl/npl-thought.ts`).

children.name: npl-thought

tags.name: sem-audiences
tags.summary: Closes the forward declaration in `spec/extraction.md` §7.
tags.description: Closes the forward declaration in `spec/extraction.md` §7. Two halves, one contract: a **declaration block** names the profiles a document knows about, and an **`audience` qualifier** on any content element says which of those profiles the element is for. The reader picks a profile; the script hides what is not for them. Nothing is ever removed from the document, and extraction never looks at the result.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: (required, document-unique): the profile token that `audience` specs and the hash parameter refer to. It is an ordinary element id, so it shares the document's id space.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: (optional): human label; the id renders when absent.

attributes.name: implies
attributes.description: (optional, comma list): profiles this one satisfies as well. `operator implies reader` means an operator sees reader content. Closure is transitive; a cycle is an authoring error, warned once and broken.

tags.example:
<sem-audiences>
  <sem-profile id="reader" label="Reader"></sem-profile>
  <sem-profile id="operator" label="Operator" implies="reader"></sem-profile>
</sem-audiences>

tags.name: sem-chronology
tags.summary: An ordered sequence of dated events — a timeline.
tags.description: An ordered sequence of dated events — a timeline. Each `sem-event` is one dated assertion: *at `when` (until `until`), this happened*, optionally carrying a lifecycle `status`. DOM order is chronological order; the vocabulary does not sort. `view-as` selects the timeline rail or a plain list and never changes what an event means.

attributes.name: when
attributes.description: (recommended): the event's date or period start, as the author wants a machine to see it (ISO-8601 preferred, free text allowed).

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: (optional): `done | current | todo | blocked` — same vocabulary as `sem-step`. Absent means unannotated, **not** `todo`: an event is a record of something that happened, not a task.

tags.example:
<sem-chronology kind="release-history" view-as="timeline" role="list">
  <sem-event role="listitem" when="2026-03-02" status="done">
    <time datetime="2026-03-02">2 Mar 2026</time> v0.1 tagged — Lit bundle ships.
  </sem-event>
  <sem-event role="listitem" when="2026-06" until="2026-08" status="current">
    <time datetime="2026-06">Jun–Aug 2026</time> Reading-experience waves.
  </sem-event>
  <sem-event role="listitem" when="2026-Q4">Theme pipeline.</sem-event>
</sem-chronology>

attributes.name: lang
attributes.description: (optional): language token, rendered as a badge.

attributes.name: mark

children.name: pre

children.name: code
children.note: Child: **exactly one `<pre>`**, conventionally wrapping one `<code>`. The listing is the `<code>`'s text (the `<pre>`'s when no `<code>` is authored).

tags.name: sem-md
tags.summary: A block whose content is authored as **Markdown** and rendered to HTML in the browser.
tags.description: A block whose content is authored as **Markdown** and rendered to HTML in the browser. The element exists for the one kind of content that is cheaper to write as Markdown than as HTML and that a machine wants back as Markdown: tables above all, then headings, lists, emphasis, links, code and quotes. It is not a second authoring format for the vocabulary — a `sem-fact` is still written as a `sem-fact` — and it never fetches, never evaluates and never injects markup: the renderer builds DOM nodes from the parsed text, so anything that looks like HTML inside the Markdown is rendered as the characters that were typed.

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: (optional): `rendered` (default) or `raw` — the initial mode. **Mutable presentation**: the toggle rewrites `data-view-as` at runtime (the authored bare attribute is left alone) and extraction ignores it (spec/extraction.md §5c).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: (optional): a short caption rendered in the chrome.

attributes.name: controls
attributes.description: (optional): comma flags from `toggle`, `copy`; default both, also when the attribute is present but empty. Unknown flags are ignored.

tags.example:
<sem-md id="m-lifetimes" label="Token lifetimes" controls="toggle,copy">
  | Token   | Lifetime | Rotates |
  | :------ | -------: | :-----: |
  | access  | 15 min   | no      |
  | refresh | 30 days  | yes     |
</sem-md>

tags.name: sem-note
tags.summary: A callout — prose set beside the main flow (`role="note"`, light DOM, content searchable).
tags.description: A callout — prose set beside the main flow (`role="note"`, light DOM, content searchable). The body is the element's content; `variant` (`info` default | `warning` | `tip` | `danger`) selects the accent and label, `collapsed` hides the body behind a ten-word teaser that expands on click, and `view-as="margin"` floats the note as a right-gutter aside on wide viewports (inline otherwise, and in print) — CSS-only. `view-as` is never extracted: a margin note and an inline note yield the same record.

attributes.name: collapsed
attributes.description: boolean attr — the body is hidden behind a ten-word teaser (`.sem-note-summary`) that expands on click.

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: presentation only. On wide viewports the note floats right beside the prose that follows it (width `--sem-margin-width`, default 14rem), inside the container; a document whose column has a gutter pushes it out with `--sem-margin-offset`. On narrow viewports and in print it reads inline as an ordinary callout. CSS-only — no handler, no chrome, no record change.

tags.example:
<sem-note variant="warning">body HTML</sem-note>
<sem-note variant="tip" collapsed>body HTML</sem-note>

tags.name: sem-procedure
tags.summary: An ordered, status-annotated procedure.
tags.description: An ordered, status-annotated procedure. Each `sem-step` is one instruction and `status` is its lifecycle annotation (`done` | `current` | `todo` default | `blocked`); DOM order is execution order — no step-number attribute, ordinals are positional and rendered with CSS counters. Status sugar (`✅/→/❌`) is display-only: `status` is canonical. Zero-JS element — pure CSS rendering. `kind` is a free token (`runbook`, `recipe`, `migration` …).
tags.example:
<sem-procedure kind="runbook" role="list">
  <sem-step role="listitem" status="done">provision Infisical path</sem-step>
  <sem-step role="listitem" status="current">port-forward MinIO</sem-step>
  <sem-step role="listitem">run migrations</sem-step>
  <sem-step role="listitem" status="blocked">cut release — waiting on CI</sem-step>
</sem-procedure>

tags.name: sem-progress
tags.summary: A completion meter — one scalar completion assertion.
tags.description: A completion meter — one scalar completion assertion. `value` is required, canonical unit 0..1: out-of-range values clamp for rendering while the raw attribute stays untouched; `label` is optional (default `progress`). The Lit component builds a meter (track + fill + `label :: N%`); JS-off the value reads as text via CSS `attr()` — no fake bar. `status="done"` ⇔ value 1 by convention.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: **required, canonical unit 0..1.** Out-of-range values clamp for rendering; the raw attr stays untouched (machine readers see the author's value, the render shows the clamp).

tags.example:
<sem-progress value="0.62" label="coverage"
     role="meter" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="1" aria-valuenow="0.62"></sem-progress>

tags.name: sem-properties
tags.summary: A definition/properties block: a closed set of key/value assertions.
tags.description: A definition/properties block: a closed set of key/value assertions. Each `sem-property` is one pair — `key` is the term (required, free text), the property text is the value. Renders a `<dl>`-equivalent grid, zero-JS: the key column renders via CSS `attr(key)`, and each property authored as `role="definition"` + `aria-label` = the key lets AT announce the pair without JS. Compact `term :: value` sugar is display-only — `key` is canonical. Pure definition list, no copy/search chrome; `view-as="glossary"` turns the block into a glossary (term anchors get hover/focus preview popovers).

attributes.name: key
attributes.description: required, free text (the term). Property text = the value.

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: (R/W1): the block is a glossary. Each property should carry an `id`; prose elsewhere links a term with a plain anchor (`JWT`), optionally wrapping it in `` at its defining use.

tags.example:
<sem-properties kind="config">
  <sem-property key="token ttl" role="definition" aria-label="token ttl">15m</sem-property>
  <sem-property key="refresh rotation" role="definition" aria-label="refresh rotation">per use</sem-property>
  <sem-property key="storage" role="definition" aria-label="storage">httpOnly cookie</sem-property>
</sem-properties>

tags.name: sem-reader
tags.summary: The reading chrome of a long document: an outline, a reading-progress bar, and the reader-side controls a browser can offer that a printed page cannot — focus mode, type size and face, colour scheme,
tags.description: The reading chrome of a long document: an outline, a reading-progress bar, and the reader-side controls a browser can offer that a printed page cannot — focus mode, type size and face, colour scheme, print, audience. It is **chrome, not content**: it mints no record, its outline is derived from the document's headings, and a document without it loses nothing a machine could read. It exists as one element (rather than one per control) because every control shares a host, a persistence policy and an a11y contract, and because the planned `sem-themes` picker collapses into its `theme` control (R/W3 — not in this wave).

attributes.name: controls
attributes.description: (optional): comma flags, in any order, from `outline`, `progress`, `focus`, `type`, `color`, `print`, `audience`. Unknown flags (including `theme`, reserved for R/W3) are ignored. Controls render in the **canonical order** above, not in attribute order.

attributes.name: outline-depth
attributes.description: (optional): deepest heading level in the generated outline, `2`–`6`; The outline always starts at `h2` — `h1` is the document title.

children.name: nav
children.note: Child (optional): an authored `<nav aria-label="Contents">`. When present it is the outline, **used verbatim** — no ids are assigned, no list is generated, nothing inside it is rewritten. This is the JS-off table of contents.

tags.example: <sem-reader controls="outline,progress,focus,type,color,print,audience" outline-depth="3"></sem-reader>

tags.name: sem-reference
tags.summary: A numbered list of works or notes the prose cites.
tags.description: A numbered list of works or notes the prose cites. Each `sem-reference` is one citable entry with an `id`; **inline citations are plain anchors** (`<a href="#r1">`) and mint nothing. The element exists because a reference needs fields a `<li>` cannot carry (`href`, `cite`) and because backlinks and hover previews are reading affordances that need JS.

tags.name: sem-reveal
tags.summary: A Q→A disclosure, `<details>`-backed — the non-assertive counterpart to the `sem-fact` Q/A shape (a reveal is exposition, not an assertion).
tags.description: A Q→A disclosure, `<details>`-backed — the non-assertive counterpart to the `sem-fact` Q/A shape (a reveal is exposition, not an assertion). `summary` labels the closed state; when absent the first body line (max 60 chars) derives it, by the one rule in `src/shared/summary.ts` that render and extraction share. `collapsed` starts hidden; without it the reveal starts open. The Lit component wraps the element in native `<details>/<summary>` — click/keyboard toggling is native; JS-off the content is fully visible (summary as a small-caps heading).

attributes.name: summary
attributes.description: optional label. **Default: first line of body (max 60 chars) acts as summary when absent.**

attributes.name: collapsed
attributes.description: boolean attr — starts hidden (the `sem-note[collapsed]` convention carries over). Without it the reveal starts **open**.

tags.example:
<sem-reveal summary="Why not localStorage?" collapsed>
  Tokens in localStorage are readable by any script on the page…
</sem-reveal>

tags.name: sem-source
tags.summary: A transparent wrapper around ordinary SemText content that lets a reader flip between the **rendered** section and its **markup as parsed, before any enhancement** (the pre-enhancement serialisation o
tags.description: A transparent wrapper around ordinary SemText content that lets a reader flip between the **rendered** section and its **markup as parsed, before any enhancement** (the pre-enhancement serialisation of the section) of the same section. It exists for documents that teach or demonstrate the vocabulary: the reader sees what a fact deck renders as, then sees exactly what was written to get it, without a second copy of the markup that could drift. It is a wrapper, not content: it mints no record, its children extract exactly as they would without it, and a document without it loses nothing a machine could read. The verbatim source is the one thing it adds, and that is a *derived* view of the children, never a second authoring.

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: (optional): `html` (default) or `source` — the initial mode. **Mutable presentation**: the toggle rewrites `data-view-as` at runtime (the authored bare attribute is left alone), and extraction ignores it (spec/extraction.md §5c).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: (optional): a short caption rendered in the chrome.

tags.name: sem-step
tags.summary: An ordered, status-annotated procedure.
tags.description: An ordered, status-annotated procedure. Each `sem-step` is one instruction and `status` is its lifecycle annotation (`done` | `current` | `todo` default | `blocked`); DOM order is execution order — no step-number attribute, ordinals are positional and rendered with CSS counters. Status sugar (`✅/→/❌`) is display-only: `status` is canonical. Zero-JS element — pure CSS rendering. `kind` is a free token (`runbook`, `recipe`, `migration` …).
tags.example:
<sem-procedure kind="runbook" role="list">
  <sem-step role="listitem" status="done">provision Infisical path</sem-step>
  <sem-step role="listitem" status="current">port-forward MinIO</sem-step>
  <sem-step role="listitem">run migrations</sem-step>
  <sem-step role="listitem" status="blocked">cut release — waiting on CI</sem-step>
</sem-procedure>

tags.name: sem-table
tags.summary: A data table a reader can sort and filter, whose **authored `<table>` is the contract**.
tags.description: A data table a reader can sort and filter, whose **authored `<table>` is the contract**. There is no JSON payload (PRD §5 planned one; it is dropped): the markup a person reads is the data a machine reads, which is the only way the extraction invariant can hold over a surface the reader reorders. The element exists because sort and filter are interactions, and because a machine reader needs the authored row order back after the DOM has been reordered — plain `<table kind="…">` covers a table nobody sorts.

attributes.name: data-value
attributes.description: (optional, on `<td>`): the sort key for that cell when the visible text is not the key (`15 min` vs `900`). Two numeric keys compare numerically; anything else compares as text, locale-aware.

attributes.name: controls
attributes.description: (optional): comma flags from `sort`, `filter`; Unknown flags are ignored.

attributes.name: sticky
attributes.description: (boolean, optional): the header row sticks to the top of the scroll container. CSS only — works with scripts off.

children.name: table
children.note: Child: **exactly one `<table>`** with a `<thead>` whose header row uses `<th scope="col">`, one `<tbody>`, and optionally a `<caption>`. A table without a `<thead>` gets no sort control. Anything else inside the table (`<tfoot>`, `colgroup`) is left alone.
